plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE adjusted for sex and age
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 human adipose bulk RNA-seq samples (6 treated, 6 control), unpaired, single batch, with sex and age recorded but the groups not matched on age. Salmon gene-level counts of unstated length-correction state (12000 genes x 12 samples in counts.csv, plus a 13th column that is likely a gene ID/name column). Because sex and age are known covariates that could confound the treated/control comparison, both are added as fixed-effect terms in the DESeq2 design (~ sex + age_centered + condition) rather than removed from counts pre-hoc, preserving valid inference on the condition coefficient. The pipeline: (1) confirm the count-import state and, if it is a raw gene-level Salmon table with no per-sample quantification files or transcript-length table, proceed with counts as delivered while flagging that the length offset is unrecoverable; (2) sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) colored by condition, sex, and age to check for confounding or outliers before modeling; (3) minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size); (4) fit DESeq2 with design ~ sex + age_centered + condition, explicit reference levels, Wald test on the condition coefficient; (5) apeglm shrinkage of the condition log2FoldChange; (6) BH-adjusted results with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, reporting the p-value histogram and NA counts; (7) fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally), then Reactome and WikiPathways human collections (all staged locally) as secondary collections; (8) a consolidated report with fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the DE gene table (unshrunken and shrunken LFC, padj), enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions, seed). Age is treated as continuous and centered before the fit per DESeq2 best practice; sex is a factor term. No batch correction is needed since there is a single batch.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
